title_as_printed: Solubility y x 10^2 (in mole fractions) of carbon dioxide in water
pressure_note: pressure of the equilibrium vessel held constant during sampling by admitting gas from the mercury-seal head space (deadweight gauge MP-2500); total/gas partial pressure not distinguished in the paper

value.col: y x 10^2 (mole fraction CO2 in water)

row_regime_overrides.reason: 25 C is below the CO2 critical temperature and p >= 10 MPa exceeds CO2 vapour pressure, so a CO2-rich liquid phase coexists with the water-rich phase (inferred from T, p, not stated by authors)

notes: The printed table is a matrix (rows t = 25, 50, 100, 150 C; columns p = 10, 20, 40, 60, 80 MPa). Written in long form, one row per (t, p) cell, rows in order of t then p. Cells blank in the print (25 C at 60 and 80 MPa, 50 C at 80 MPa) are written as rows with empty value; the text says sampling there was difficult because CO2 was denser than water. Columns the authors call y: mole fraction of CO2 in water; salt-free (pure water). 'note' column holds no footnote letters (empty).
